clues: This city sits in the south west of Ontario, in Canada, where two rivers meet. It lies much the same trip from Toronto as from Detroit.
Strong cold winds blow in from Lake Huron, to the north west. They drag bursts of lake snow with them as they cross the cold lake.
This place began as a small village founded in 1826. Less than thirty years later, in 1855, it had grown and was made a full city.
This city and its main river took their names from a famed city and river in England. A man named Simcoe gave them those names in 1793.
Two big highways meet in this city, routes 401 and 402. They link it to Toronto, to Windsor, and to the border with the United States.
